parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks two traveller-facing exposures. Nationally, the 2025 passport regime (X-marker eliminated, M/F only per birth sex, in force since the Supreme Court's Nov 2025 order) guarantees document mismatch, driving refusal, secondary screening, stranded travellers and a possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility finding; eight governments issued advisories. In this division, from 1 July 2026 it is a crime — up to one year jail — to use any restroom or changing room not matching birth sex, reaching government buildings AND private businesses (restaurants, hospitals, gas stations): a tier-1 universal exposure. A comparable arrest ended with 24 hours in a men's ward. Immigration/corrections custody documents abuse. Remedy exists (pending suit, one narrowing ruling) but its status is unknown.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: passport X-markers and non-birth-sex markers stopped Feb 2025; M/F only per supporting documents; Nov 2025 court allowed restriction. Discrepancy cable instructs refusal and additional evidence; possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility finding. Trans travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and being stranded abroad; multiple foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waiver; existing X passports valid to expiry; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal document mismatch feeds state-level exposure: an outed or discrepant visitor carries the same mismatch into division restroom enforcement and any ID check.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: trans woman arrested 19 March 2025 under a comparable state law, handcuffed, held 24 hours in the men's ward. Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; federal corrections from 2026 mandates conversion-therapy-style regime (hair cut, hormones removed) and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest. Trans prisoners may receive hormone therapy under a Sept 2024 national ruling nullifying a 1997 ban. Habeas/courts function (injunctions issued).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry-document discrepancy → investigation/fraud allegation → detention → birth-sex placement; the documented men's-ward hold shows the chain operating end-to-end.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented: division law effective 1 July 2026 criminalises birth-sex-mismatched restroom/changing-room use in government buildings AND public-facing private businesses (gas stations, restaurants, entertainment venues, hospitals), first offence misdemeanour up to one year. Nationally 10 units ban gender-congruent facility use in all government buildings; 4 units criminalise it in circumstances. This is the only such law reaching private businesses, with steepest penalties.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Suit filed 30 April 2026 (due process, equal protection, privacy) with six trans plaintiffs; a district judge issued a 16 June 2026 narrowing; 29 units plus capital district have no mapped ban; trespass triggers require refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal division exposure combines with federal document mismatch: any ID check, hospital visit or emergency can convert a document discrepancy into a criminal facility charge; hospital ward placement intersects with the hospital reach of the ban.

care_services.exposure: Documented: hospitals are within the division's criminal facility reach; federal executive orders frame minor gender-affirming care as 'mutilation', restrict funding, and a March 2026 division law forces disclosure of a trans minor's status to parents within three days by schools, childcare and medical professionals; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records from 20+ hospitals.
care_services.protection: Pending challenges to the October 2025 proposed health rules and several executive orders; some orders enjoined; hormone therapy protected for prisoners nationally since Sept 2024.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces disclosure mandates and criminalised facility use inside care settings; an adult's own document mismatch can surface during medical care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: executive orders and a counterterrorism strategy naming 'radically pro-transgender' ideologies among prioritised targets; 'radical gender ideology' cited among violent-extremist animating views; reward system for identifying extremist leadership; gender-ideology 'forbidden terms' purge; 66% of residents back sex-at-birth document rules; advocates invoke genocide-stage comparison.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memorandum never lists 'radical gender ideology' as a reward criterion; the counterterrorism document says powers will not target mere disagreement; national employment-discrimination and gender-identity hate-crime statutes remain in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing raises the probability that a document discrepancy or facility encounter escalates to referral rather than a warning.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: March 2026 division law requires schools, childcare and medical professionals to disclose a trans minor's status to parents within three days; executive order threatens criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; minor care bans in 27 units; a blocked 2022 bill sought felony/life terms for parents taking children out-of-state for care.
minors_guardians.protection: The 2022 parental felony bill died in the upper chamber; litigation continues against federal orders; national hate-crime statute covers minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: For an adult travelling with a minor, the restroom criminalisation applies independently to each traveller; disclosure mandates bite if either seeks school, childcare or medical contact.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: no division-specific data showing trans violence materially above the general homicide rate was found; a documented arrest with men's-ward detention shows police enforcing facility law against a trans person; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes; 2023 counted 190+ anti-trans bills.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling; municipal/county ordinances cover ~40% of the division's population; a national risk assessment flags 4 'Do Not Travel' units but not this one.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin recourse at state level means a street assault investigation depends on federal hate-crime machinery and local police disposition.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Not documented: no enforcement action under the division measure against a visitor or resident identified; unresolved felony/misdemeanour classification discrepancy; unknown whether the 16 June 2026 narrowing stands; litigation outcomes unresolved nationally.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented: active, partly successful litigation (injunctions, a narrowing ruling, fee awards), a functioning legal-aid FAQ, national hate-crime and employment protections, courts granting relief to trans litigants.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts mitigate only where they have ruled; here several key rulings' current status is unknown, so paper and pending relief cannot be credited as operating protection.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: Vellandra merely refuses entry and expels without arrest or charge. Here the traveller faces an actual criminal statute (up to one year) reaching essentially every restroom, including private restaurants and hospitals, plus documented arrest under an analogous law with men's-ward detention, alongside federal document refusal. Worse than exclusion-only, so below 0.35.

Somewhat higher than 0.25-C: Ostravia's birth-sex prison placement and cross-dressing arrest recur with slow remedies, but its sentences are brief, execution barred, and no capital pathway. This division adds a broader criminal reach (private businesses, up to a year) but has no documented recurring custody abuse of visitors, no raids, and courts granting partial relief — net a step above 0.25.

Materially lower than 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles' worst outcome is discretionary refusal of admission and returned transport with written decisions and appeal desks, no criminal exposure. Here entry scrutiny can trigger a fraud/lifetime-ineligibility finding, and everyday facility use inside the division is itself a misdemeanour. Severity and universality both exceed the 0.55 profile.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a federal document regime that guarantees mismatch and can refuse entry or allege fraud, stacked on a division that criminalises birth-sex-mismatched restroom use in every government building and public-facing private business from 1 July 2026 — a universal, state-enforced exposure covering restaurants, gas stations and hospitals, with up to a year in jail. An analogous arrest already produced a 24-hour hold in a men's ward, demonstrating the document→custody→birth-sex-placement chain. Immigration and corrections custody document abuse. Mitigation is real but unconfirmed: a pending suit, an unresolved narrowing ruling, federal hate-crime and employment statutes, and functioning courts that have granted trans litigants relief. Absent documented enforcement against visitors or trans-specific violence above baseline, this sits in High Risk, near the 0.35 boundary rather than the 0.25 tier.
